hypothesis: Combining the best RAG generator (exp011) with a richer composite deterministic selector — penalising filler, near-duplicates, and compound questions while rewarding coverage span — should beat exp011 and fix exp004's atomicity-blind coverage-only scoring, because the multi-dimensional shape ruler better approximates true set quality.
technique: Four candidate sets are drawn from the exp011 contrastive-RAG generator at a low-temperature floor [0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0]; a fully deterministic Swift composite ruler (CoverageScorer span − FillerDetector − Jaccard near-dup penalty − compound-question penalty) selects the best-shaped set with no model-based judgment.
result: Scored 0.297 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), −0.026 below the exp011 best of 0.323 and −0.010 below the 0.307 baseline; rubric atom=4, spec=3, cover=3, nat=3, nonRed=4. The composite ruler did improve non-redundancy (nonRed 4) but coverage stayed pinned at 3, and crucially the shape-based selector actively preferred a catastrophic context-leakage draw (garage questions for a dinner-party task) because it scored high on coverage span with no task-fit signal — discarded.
